segments.label: §52, de source block1
segments.text: Die Nationen verändern ihre Sprachen auch bloss durch sich selbst, ohne Abzweigung und Mischung, in ihrem gemeinsamen Fortleben beständig, und nach grösseren Zeiträumen werden diese Aenderungen bemerkbar.

segments.label: §52, de source block2
segments.text: Umfang, Schnelligkeit und Art dieser Umänderungen hängen von der Lebendigkeit des Sprachverkehrs, und von der Tiefe ab, mit welcher der Mensch den Gehalt der Sprache erfasst.

segments.label: §52, de source block3
segments.text: Denn wir werden weiter unten sehen, dass es hierin verschiedene Grade giebt.

segments.label: §52, de source block4
segments.text: Auf diese Umänderungen zu achten, ist ein hauptsächliches Geschäft der Sprachforschung.

segments.label: §52, de source block5
segments.text: Aber auch wo die Sprache durch Abzweigung und Mischung gewaltsamer umgeformt wird, wirkt die nationelle Individualitaet vorzugsweise ein nach der Art, wie das Fremde sie berührt, und wie sie dasselbe mit der ihr inwohnenden Kraft bearbeitet.

segments.label: §52, de source block6
segments.text: Es bedarf indess kaum der Erinnerung, dass, um sich diesen nationellen Einfluss klar zu machen, man auf jene eigne Behandlung der Sprache durch den Einzelnen zurückgehen muss, die in demselben nur als Masse erscheint.

segments.label: §52, de source block7
segments.text: Allein auch innerhalb einer Nation weicht bisweilen ein Einzelner von dem durch Alle gegebenen Gange ab, und macht durch eine plötzlich in ihm aufleuchtende Ansicht, durch eine entscheidende Erfindung, oder durch seine eigenthümliche Manier die Sprache zu brauchen eine neue Weise der Sprachbehandlung geltend.

segments.label: §52, de source block8
segments.text: Denn obgleich der Intellectualitaet der Nationen, ebenso wie der des Menschengeschlechts, Gränzen gesteckt sind, so bleibt doch auch da dem Individuum ein gewisser Spielraum vorbehalten.

segments.label: §52, de source block9
segments.text: Ueberall, wo die Freiheit sich in Schranken der Endlichkeit bewegt, giebt es zwar eine Reihe bestimmender, ihr im Augenblick des Wirkens fremder Einflüsse, sie kann aber auch, wie ein Blitz aus dem wolkenlosen Aether, plötzlich aus denselben heraustreten, und selbstbestimmend werden.

segments.label: §52, codex source block1
segments.text: Nations also continually change their languages purely through themselves, without branching off or mixture, in the continuing course of their common life; these changes become perceptible after longer periods.

segments.label: §52, codex source block2
segments.text: The extent, speed and manner of these transformations depend on the liveliness of linguistic intercourse and the depth with which human beings grasp the content of language.

segments.label: §52, codex source block3
segments.text: For we shall see below that there are different degrees in this.

segments.label: §52, codex source block4
segments.text: Attending to these transformations is a principal task of linguistic research.

segments.label: §52, codex source block5
segments.text: But even where language is more violently reshaped through branching off and mixture, national individuality exercises a predominant influence according to the way the foreign element touches it and the way it works upon that element with its inherent power.

segments.label: §52, codex source block6
segments.text: It scarcely needs recalling, however, that to make this national influence clear to ourselves, we must go back to the individual's distinctive treatment of language, which appears in that influence only in the aggregate.

segments.label: §52, codex source block7
segments.text: Yet even within a nation, an individual sometimes departs from the course given by everyone and establishes a new way of treating language through an insight suddenly flashing upon him, through a decisive invention, or through his distinctive manner of using language.

segments.label: §52, codex source block8
segments.text: For although limits are set to the intellectuality of nations, as to that of the human race, a certain latitude remains reserved for the individual even here.

segments.label: §52, codex source block9
segments.text: Wherever freedom moves within the bounds of finitude, there is certainly a series of determining influences alien to it at the moment of action; yet, like lightning from a cloudless ether, it can also suddenly emerge from them and become self-determining.

segments.label: §52, muse source block2
segments.text: Extent, rapidity and manner of these alterations depend on the liveliness of linguistic intercourse and on the depth with which man grasps the content of language.

segments.label: §52, muse source block3
segments.text: For we shall see further below that in this respect there are different degrees.

segments.label: §52, muse source block4
segments.text: To pay attention to these alterations is a principal business of research into language.

segments.label: §52, muse source block5
segments.text: But also where language is more violently transformed through branching off and mixture, national individuality acts pre-eminently according to the manner in which what is foreign touches it, and in which it works upon the foreign element with the power dwelling in it.

segments.label: §52, muse source block6
segments.text: There is, however, hardly need of the reminder that, in order to make this national influence clear to oneself, one must go back to that peculiar treatment of language by the individual which appears in it only as a mass.

segments.label: §52, muse source block7
segments.text: But also within a nation an individual sometimes deviates from the course given through all, and through a view suddenly lighting up in him, through a decisive invention, or through his peculiar manner of using language, makes a new manner of treating language prevail.

segments.label: §52, muse source block8

segments.label: §53, de source block1
segments.text: Darauf beruht es, dass in der Menschheit und in dem tieferregten Menschen ein unaufhörliches Schaffen lebendig ist, dass sich die Art ihres Seyns nie weder berechnen, noch erschöpfend erklären lässt, da jeder Richtung das unerklärbare Princip der Freiheit beigemischt bleibt.

segments.label: §53, de source block2
segments.text: In den Sprachen rührt es daher, dass sie unerwartet plötzliche Aufflüge nehmen, und sogar nicht einmal immer allmählich herabsinken, dass an sich gleichartige bei verschiedenen Nationen so verschiedene Behandlung erfahren, dass sie grosse Verschiedenheit des Charakters zeigen, wie z. B. die Griechische und Lateinische, dass einzelne Schriftsteller ganz neue Epochen ihrer Behandlungsart gründen, was auch gewiss schon vor Erfindung der Schrift geschieht, nur da sich für die Nachwelt in Dunkel verliert.

segments.label: §53, codex source block1
segments.text: On this rests the fact that an unceasing creation is alive in humanity and in the deeply stirred human being, and that the manner of their being can never be calculated or exhaustively explained, since the inexplicable principle of freedom remains mingled into every direction it takes.

segments.label: §53, codex source block2
segments.text: In languages, this is why they unexpectedly take sudden flights upwards and do not even always decline gradually; why languages alike in kind in themselves receive such different treatment among different nations that they display great diversity of character, as Greek and Latin do, for example; and why individual writers inaugurate entirely new epochs in the manner of treating them—something that certainly also occurs before the invention of writing, but there is lost in darkness for posterity.

segments.label: §53, muse source block1
segments.text: On this it rests that in mankind and in the deeply moved human being an incessant creating is alive, that the manner of their being can never be either calculated or exhaustively explained, since the inexplicable principle of freedom remains mixed into every direction.

segments.label: §53, muse source block2
segments.text: In languages it comes from this that they take unexpected sudden flights upward, and do not even always gradually sink down, that languages in themselves of the same kind experience such different treatment among different nations, that they show great diversity of character, as for example Greek and Latin, and that individual writers found wholly new epochs in the manner of treating them, which certainly also happened before the invention of writing, only there it loses itself in darkness for posterity.

segments.label: §53, astra source block1
segments.text: This is the ground of the unceasing creation alive in humanity and in the deeply stirred individual, and of the impossibility of ever calculating or exhaustively explaining the manner of their being, since the inexplicable principle of freedom remains mingled with every direction they take.

segments.text: In languages, this is why they unexpectedly take sudden flights upwards and do not even always sink gradually; why languages alike in kind in themselves receive such different treatment among different nations that they display great differences of character, as Greek and Latin do, for example; and why individual writers inaugurate entirely new epochs in the manner of their treatment. This last certainly also happens before the invention of writing, but there it is lost in obscurity for posterity.

segments.label: §54, de source block1
segments.text: Der Sprachforschung wird diese Rücksicht vorzüglich darum wichtig, darin eine Warnung gegen das Ausreichen bloss mechanischer Erklärungsarten, und gegen das zu grosse Vertrauen auf analytisches Verfahren zu finden.

segments.label: §54, de source block2
segments.text: Sie muss allerdings dem gleichförmigen Gange nachspähen, welchen der Mensch bei Umänderung und Bildung der Sprache nimmt, aber nur mit Rücksicht auf die selbständige Kraft, die denselben zu verlassen, oder ihn abzukürzen vermag, deren blosser Anhauch den Sprachstoffen eine ganz verschiedene Natur giebt; man muss allerdings zergliedern und aus einander herleiten, aber nur mit dem Gefühl, dass es auch wahre Synthesen giebt, wo Idee und Laut auf einem Wege, dem nicht weiter nachgeforscht werden kann, zusammentreffen.

segments.label: §54, de source block3
segments.text: Wie der Vorrath von Wörtern und das System von Regeln, welche wir Sprache nennen, immer im Denken, Sprechen und Aufzeichnen von dem lebendigen Geiste befruchtet werden, so muss auch die Untersuchung den lebendigen Geist und die todte Sprache immer zugleich vor Augen haben, und ihrer Wechselwirkung nachgehen.

segments.label: §54, de source block4
segments.text: Die Individualitaet der Nationen kann so mannigfaltige Wege einschlagen, dass jeder Versuch, sie auch nur in Gattungen zu fassen, vergeblich seyn würde.

segments.label: §54, de source block5
segments.text: Aber für die hauptsächlichsten Einwirkungen auf die Sprache kommt es immer nur auf die beiden Punkte an: ob sie sich überhaupt und von welcher Seite aus zur Intellectualitaet, und ob gerade zur Intellectualitaet durch Sprache neigt ?

segments.label: §54, de source block6
segments.text: Denn wie man im täglichen Leben verschiedene Grade und Arten der Sprachbedürftigkeit, des Sprachgefühls, der Sprachbehandlung unter den Menschen antrift, so ist es auch mit den Nationen, und was in der beständigen Fortbildung der Sprachen erscheint, das ist auch bei ihrer Entstehung aus einander geschehen, da diese ja selbst (43.) nur ein allmähliches Anderswerden seyn konnte.

segments.label: §54, de source block7
segments.text: Ueber diese Verschiedenheit der nationellen Aneignung der Sprache liesse sich noch Vieles bemerken, wenn es nicht mein Zweck in diesem Kapitel wäre, um den Bau und das Ineinandergreifen des Ganzen zu zeigen, das Einzelne bloss andeutungsweise zu berühren.

segments.label: §54, codex source block1
segments.text: This consideration becomes especially important for linguistic research as a warning against treating merely mechanical modes of explanation as sufficient and placing excessive trust in analytical procedure.

segments.label: §54, codex source block2
segments.text: Research must certainly trace the uniform course human beings take in transforming and forming language, but only with regard for the independent power capable of leaving that course or shortening it, whose mere breath gives linguistic materials an entirely different nature; one must certainly analyse and derive one thing from another, but only with the feeling that there are also true syntheses, in which idea and sound meet by a route that cannot be investigated further.

segments.label: §54, codex source block3
segments.text: Just as the stock of words and system of rules we call language are always fertilised by the living mind in thinking, speaking and recording, so investigation too must always keep both the living mind and dead language in view and follow their interaction.

segments.label: §54, codex source block4
segments.text: The individuality of nations can take such manifold paths that any attempt even to comprehend it in classes would be vain.

segments.label: §54, codex source block5
segments.text: But for the principal influences on language, only two points ever matter: whether national individuality inclines towards intellectuality at all, and from what side; and whether it inclines specifically towards intellectuality through language.

segments.label: §54, codex source block6
segments.text: For just as in daily life we encounter different degrees and kinds of need for language, feeling for language and treatment of language among individuals, so too with nations; and what manifests itself in the continual further development of languages also occurred in their emergence from one another, since this itself (43) could only have been a gradual becoming different.

segments.label: §54, codex source block7
segments.text: Much more could be observed about this diversity in the national appropriation of language, were it not my purpose in this chapter to touch on particulars only by way of indication, in order to show the structure and interlocking of the whole.

segments.text: This consideration becomes important for research into language pre-eminently because a warning is to be found in it against the sufficiency of merely mechanical kinds of explanation and against too great trust in analytical procedure.

segments.text: But for the principal influences upon language it always matters only to know the two points: whether it inclines at all, and from which side, to intellectuality, and whether it inclines precisely to intellectuality through language?

segments.text: Just as the stock of words and system of rules we call language are always fertilized by the living mind in thinking, speaking and recording, investigation too must always keep the living mind and dead language before it together, and follow their interaction.

segments.label: §54, revised source block4
segments.text: The individuality of nations can take such manifold paths that any attempt even to group it into classes would be futile.

segments.label: §54, revised source block5
segments.text: But for the principal influences upon language, only two points ever matter: whether national individuality inclines towards intellectual life at all, and from what direction; and whether it inclines specifically towards intellectual life through language.

segments.label: §54, revised source block6
segments.text: For just as in everyday life we encounter different degrees and kinds of need for language, feeling for language and treatment of language among human beings, so it is with nations; and what appears in the continual further development of languages also occurred when they arose from one another, since this emergence itself (43) could only have been a gradual becoming different.

segments.label: §54, revised source block7
segments.text: Much more could be said about this diversity in the national appropriation of language, were it not my purpose in this chapter to touch on particulars only by way of indication, so as to show the structure and interlocking of the whole.

segments.label: §55, de source block1
segments.text: Da wir nunmehr die Sprache überhaupt in ihrer zwiefachen Natur betrachtet haben, als geistigen Act im Sprechen und Verstehen, und als durch diesen erzeugten, todten, zwar nie ausser dem Menschen, aber immer ausser dem Einzelnen vorhandenen Stoff (40 — 54.) , da wir ferner in ihr den Naturzusammenhang (40 — 51.) getrennt haben von der nationellen und individuellen Freiheit (52 — 54.), so gehen wir jetzt zu ihrem Verfahren im Einzelnen über.

segments.label: §55, de source block2
segments.text: In diesem sondern sich nun zwei Dinge deutlich von einander ab, die Wörter und die Redeverbindung, als die Materie und Form der Sprache.

segments.label: §55, de source block3
segments.text: Man muss diese Eintheilung nicht verwechseln mit der in Laute und Regeln; denn auch die Wortbildung kennt Regeln, und die Redeverbindung bedient sich bisweilen ihr eigenthümlicher Laute ; man muss vielmehr, die Rede als den Zweck der Sprache betrachtend, diese Classification dergestalt in ihrer wahren Natur fest halten, dass der eine Theil die Elemente, der andre die Verbindung der Rede behandelt.

segments.label: §55, de source block4
segments.text: Da aber beiden der Laut gemeinsam ist, so muss die Betrachtung des Lautsystems vorausgeschickt werden.

segments.label: §55, codex source block1
segments.text: Having now considered language in general in its twofold nature, as a mental act in speaking and understanding, and as dead material produced through that act, material which never exists outside human beings but always exists outside the individual (40–54); and having further distinguished within it the natural nexus (40–51) from national and individual freedom (52–54), we now turn to its procedure in detail.

segments.label: §55, codex source block2
segments.text: Here two things clearly separate from one another: words and the connection of discourse, as the matter and form of language.

segments.label: §55, codex source block3
segments.text: This division must not be confused with the division into sounds and rules, for word formation too has rules, and the connection of discourse sometimes employs sounds peculiar to it; rather, regarding discourse as the purpose of language, we must hold firmly to the true nature of this classification, so that one part treats the elements of discourse and the other their connection.

segments.label: §55, codex source block4
segments.text: Since sound is common to both, however, an examination of the sound system must precede them.

segments.label: §55, muse source block1
segments.text: Since we have now considered language in general in its twofold nature, as a mental act in speaking and understanding and as dead material produced through that act, material present indeed never outside man but always outside the individual (40 — 54.), and since we have further separated in it the natural connexion (40 — 51.) from national and individual freedom (52 — 54.), we now pass to its procedure in particulars.

segments.label: §55, muse source block2
segments.text: In this procedure two things now clearly separate themselves from each other, words and the combination of speech, as the matter and form of language.

segments.label: §55, muse source block3
segments.text: This division must not be confused with that into sounds and rules; for word-formation too knows rules, and the combination of speech sometimes makes use of sounds peculiar to it; rather, regarding speech as the purpose of language, one must hold fast to this classification in its true nature in such a way that the one part treats the elements of speech and the other its combination.

segments.label: §55, muse source block4
segments.text: But since sound is common to both, consideration of the system of sounds must be placed in front.

segments.label: §55, astra source block1
segments.text: Now that we have considered language in general in its twofold nature—as a mental act in speaking and understanding, and as the lifeless material produced by that act, which never exists outside human beings but always exists outside the individual (40–54)—and have further distinguished its natural interconnectedness (40–51) from national and individual freedom (52–54), we shall turn to its procedure in detail.

segments.label: §55, astra source block2
segments.text: Two things now stand clearly apart within this procedure: words and the combination of discourse, as the matter and form of language.

segments.label: §55, astra source block3
segments.text: This division must not be confused with that into sounds and rules, for word formation too has rules, and the combination of discourse sometimes employs sounds peculiar to itself. Rather, regarding discourse as the purpose of language, we must hold firmly to the true nature of this classification: one part treats the elements of discourse, the other their combination.

segments.label: §55, astra source block4
segments.text: But since sound is common to both, consideration of the sound system must come first.

segments.label: §55, synthesis source block1
segments.text: Now that we have considered language in general in its twofold nature—as a mental act in speaking and understanding, and as the dead material produced by that act, which never exists outside human beings but always exists outside the individual (40–54)—and have further distinguished its natural interconnectedness (40–51) from national and individual freedom (52–54), we shall turn to its procedure in detail.

segments.label: §55, synthesis source block2
segments.text: Two things now stand clearly apart within this procedure: words and the combining of words into discourse, as the matter and form of language.

segments.label: §55, synthesis source block3
segments.text: This division must not be confused with that into sounds and rules, for word formation too has rules, and the combining of words into discourse sometimes employs sounds peculiar to itself. Rather, regarding discourse as the purpose of language, we must hold firmly to the true nature of this classification: one part treats the elements of discourse, the other their combination.
