text_version.title: Grundzüge §50 — checked German

text_version.body: To leave nothing wanting in the precise delimitation of concepts, however, we must add to the foregoing that the individuality of a language can itself be individuality only comparatively, and that true individuality lies only in the person speaking on each occasion. In fact, only this completes the concept. A nation certainly has, on the whole, the same language; yet not even all its members have precisely the same one (38), and if we proceed further into the finest detail, each human being possesses a language of his own. No one thinks exactly what another does on hearing a word, and the difference, however small, trembles through the entire language, if we may compare language with the most mobile of all the elements. In every act of thinking and feeling, the same difference recurs by virtue of the sameness of the individuality, forming a mass out of things individually imperceptible. All understanding is therefore always at the same time a not-understanding—a truth that can also be put to excellent use in practical life—and all agreement in thoughts and feelings is at the same time a divergence. This remains invisible only where it hides beneath the generality of concept and feeling; but where heightened power breaks through that generality and individualises more sharply even for consciousness, it comes clearly to light. Thus no one will deny that every significant writer has a language of his own. It may admittedly be objected that by language we mean precisely that generality of forms, words and rules which allows room for diverse individuality, and this is certainly perfectly true. Nevertheless, the view raised here cannot on that account be banished even from the domain of the most general investigation of language. For there are several levels at which the generality of linguistic forms is individualised in this way, and the individualising principle is the same: thinking and speaking within a particular individuality. This gives rise to diversity in the language of individuals as of nations. Everywhere it is only a matter of more or less. We must therefore descend to the final level. One might admittedly wish to find the boundary where language, though individually nuanced, nevertheless employs the same sounds. But even among the different classes of a nation this is not entirely the case; and the individual too uses some preferentially, employs others as though they were foreign to him, excludes still others altogether, and thereby forms his own dictionary, quite apart from divergences in meaning.

Thereby arises the diversity in the language of individuals as of nations. Everywhere it is only a more or less. One must therefore descend to the last stage. text_version.title: Grundzüge §50 — revised English, nature of language

text_version.body: Vorzüglich aber ist nothwendig, auf die Modificirung der Sprache in jedem Individuum aufmerksam zu machen, um die Gewalt des Menschen über die Sprache zu beweisen, so wie wir im Vorigen (42. 43.) ihre Macht über ihn dargestellt haben. Diese kann man (wenn man den Ausdruck auf geistige Kräfte anwenden will) als ein physiologisches Wirken ansehen, jene ist ein rein dynamisches, in dieser liegt die Natur der wirkenden Kräfte der Sprache, in jener das Princip ihrer Freiheit. Denn es kann im Menschen etwas aufsteigen, dessen Grund kein Verstand in den vorhergehenden Zuständen aufzufinden vermag, und man würde die Natur der Sprache verkennen, und gerade die geschichtliche Wahrheit ihrer Entstehung und Umänderung verletzen, wenn man die Möglichkeit solcher unerklärbaren Erscheinungen von ihr ausschliessen wollte. Wenn aber auch die Freiheit unbestimmbar und unerklärbar ist, so lassen sich, nur innerhalb eines gewissen Spielraums, ihre Gränzen erkennen, und die Sprachuntersuchung muss die Erscheinung der Freiheit erkennen und ehren, aber ihren Gränzen sorgfältig nachspüren, um nicht in den Sprachen durch Freiheit für möglich zu halten, was es nicht ist.

text_version.body: Above all, however, attention must be drawn to the modification of language in each individual, in order to demonstrate human power over language, just as we presented its power over human beings above (42, 43). The latter may be regarded as a physiological operation, if one wishes to apply the expression to mental powers; the former is a purely dynamic operation: in the latter lies the nature of the operative powers of language, in the former the principle of their freedom. For something may arise in a human being whose ground no understanding can discover in preceding states; and we would misunderstand the nature of language, and violate precisely the historical truth of its genesis and transformation, if we sought to exclude from it the possibility of such inexplicable phenomena. Yet although freedom cannot be determined or explained, its limits can be recognised, albeit only within a certain latitude; linguistic investigation must recognise and honour the manifestation of freedom, but carefully trace its limits, so as not to regard as possible in languages through freedom what is not possible.

text_version.body: Pre-eminently, however, it is necessary to draw attention to the modification of language in every individual in order to prove the power of man over language, just as in what precedes (42. 43.) we have presented its might over him. The latter can be regarded (if one wants to apply the expression to mental powers) as a physiological working; the former is a purely dynamical one; in the latter lies the nature of the working powers of language, in the former the principle of its freedom. For something can arise in man whose ground no understanding can discover in preceding states, and one would misconceive the nature of language, and precisely violate the historical truth of its origin and alteration, if one wanted to exclude the possibility of such inexplicable appearances from it. But even if freedom is indeterminable and inexplicable, its limits can be recognized, though only within a certain latitude, and investigation of language must recognize and honour the appearance of freedom, but carefully trace its limits, so as not to regard as possible through freedom in languages what is not so.

text_version.title: Grundzüge §51 — revised English, nature of language

text_version.body: Die Nationen verändern ihre Sprachen auch bloss durch sich selbst, ohne Abzweigung und Mischung, in ihrem gemeinsamen Fortleben beständig, und nach grösseren Zeiträumen werden diese Aenderungen bemerkbar. Umfang, Schnelligkeit und Art dieser Umänderungen hängen von der Lebendigkeit des Sprachverkehrs, und von der Tiefe ab, mit welcher der Mensch den Gehalt der Sprache erfasst. Denn wir werden weiter unten sehen, dass es hierin verschiedene Grade giebt. Auf diese Umänderungen zu achten, ist ein hauptsächliches Geschäft der Sprachforschung. Aber auch wo die Sprache durch Abzweigung und Mischung gewaltsamer umgeformt wird, wirkt die nationelle Individualitaet vorzugsweise ein nach der Art, wie das Fremde sie berührt, und wie sie dasselbe mit der ihr inwohnenden Kraft bearbeitet. Es bedarf indess kaum der Erinnerung, dass, um sich diesen nationellen Einfluss klar zu machen, man auf jene eigne Behandlung der Sprache durch den Einzelnen zurückgehen muss, die in demselben nur als Masse erscheint. Allein auch innerhalb einer Nation weicht bisweilen ein Einzelner von dem durch Alle gegebenen Gange ab, und macht durch eine plötzlich in ihm aufleuchtende Ansicht, durch eine entscheidende Erfindung, oder durch seine eigenthümliche Manier die Sprache zu brauchen eine neue Weise der Sprachbehandlung geltend. Denn obgleich der Intellectualitaet der Nationen, ebenso wie der des Menschengeschlechts, Gränzen gesteckt sind, so bleibt doch auch da dem Individuum ein gewisser Spielraum vorbehalten. Ueberall, wo die Freiheit sich in Schranken der Endlichkeit bewegt, giebt es zwar eine Reihe bestimmender, ihr im Augenblick des Wirkens fremder Einflüsse, sie kann aber auch, wie ein Blitz aus dem wolkenlosen Aether, plötzlich aus denselben heraustreten, und selbstbestimmend werden.

text_version.title: Grundzüge §52 — checked German

text_version.body: Nations also continually change their languages purely through themselves, without branching off or mixture, in the continuing course of their common life; these changes become perceptible after longer periods. The extent, speed and manner of these transformations depend on the liveliness of linguistic intercourse and the depth with which human beings grasp the content of language. For we shall see below that there are different degrees in this. Attending to these transformations is a principal task of linguistic research. But even where language is more violently reshaped through branching off and mixture, national individuality exercises a predominant influence according to the way the foreign element touches it and the way it works upon that element with its inherent power. It scarcely needs recalling, however, that to make this national influence clear to ourselves, we must go back to the individual's distinctive treatment of language, which appears in that influence only in the aggregate. Yet even within a nation, an individual sometimes departs from the course given by everyone and establishes a new way of treating language through an insight suddenly flashing upon him, through a decisive invention, or through his distinctive manner of using language. For although limits are set to the intellectuality of nations, as to that of the human race, a certain latitude remains reserved for the individual even here. Wherever freedom moves within the bounds of finitude, there is certainly a series of determining influences alien to it at the moment of action; yet, like lightning from a cloudless ether, it can also suddenly emerge from them and become self-determining.

text_version.body: Darauf beruht es, dass in der Menschheit und in dem tieferregten Menschen ein unaufhörliches Schaffen lebendig ist, dass sich die Art ihres Seyns nie weder berechnen, noch erschöpfend erklären lässt, da jeder Richtung das unerklärbare Princip der Freiheit beigemischt bleibt. In den Sprachen rührt es daher, dass sie unerwartet plötzliche Aufflüge nehmen, und sogar nicht einmal immer allmählich herabsinken, dass an sich gleichartige bei verschiedenen Nationen so verschiedene Behandlung erfahren, dass sie grosse Verschiedenheit des Charakters zeigen, wie z. B. die Griechische und Lateinische, dass einzelne Schriftsteller ganz neue Epochen ihrer Behandlungsart gründen, was auch gewiss schon vor Erfindung der Schrift geschieht, nur da sich für die Nachwelt in Dunkel verliert.

text_version.title: Grundzüge §53 — checked German

text_version.body: On this rests the fact that an unceasing creation is alive in humanity and in the deeply stirred human being, and that the manner of their being can never be calculated or exhaustively explained, since the inexplicable principle of freedom remains mingled into every direction it takes. In languages, this is why they unexpectedly take sudden flights upwards and do not even always decline gradually; why languages alike in kind in themselves receive such different treatment among different nations that they display great diversity of character, as Greek and Latin do, for example; and why individual writers inaugurate entirely new epochs in the manner of treating them—something that certainly also occurs before the invention of writing, but there is lost in darkness for posterity.

text_version.title: Grundzüge §53 — revised English, nature of language

text_version.body: Der Sprachforschung wird diese Rücksicht vorzüglich darum wichtig, darin eine Warnung gegen das Ausreichen bloss mechanischer Erklärungsarten, und gegen das zu grosse Vertrauen auf analytisches Verfahren zu finden. Sie muss allerdings dem gleichförmigen Gange nachspähen, welchen der Mensch bei Umänderung und Bildung der Sprache nimmt, aber nur mit Rücksicht auf die selbständige Kraft, die denselben zu verlassen, oder ihn abzukürzen vermag, deren blosser Anhauch den Sprachstoffen eine ganz verschiedene Natur giebt; man muss allerdings zergliedern und aus einander herleiten, aber nur mit dem Gefühl, dass es auch wahre Synthesen giebt, wo Idee und Laut auf einem Wege, dem nicht weiter nachgeforscht werden kann, zusammentreffen. Wie der Vorrath von Wörtern und das System von Regeln, welche wir Sprache nennen, immer im Denken, Sprechen und Aufzeichnen von dem lebendigen Geiste befruchtet werden, so muss auch die Untersuchung den lebendigen Geist und die todte Sprache immer zugleich vor Augen haben, und ihrer Wechselwirkung nachgehen. Die Individualitaet der Nationen kann so mannigfaltige Wege einschlagen, dass jeder Versuch, sie auch nur in Gattungen zu fassen, vergeblich seyn würde. Aber für die hauptsächlichsten Einwirkungen auf die Sprache kommt es immer nur auf die beiden Punkte an: ob sie sich überhaupt und von welcher Seite aus zur Intellectualitaet, und ob gerade zur Intellectualitaet durch Sprache neigt ? Denn wie man im täglichen Leben verschiedene Grade und Arten der Sprachbedürftigkeit, des Sprachgefühls, der Sprachbehandlung unter den Menschen antrift, so ist es auch mit den Nationen, und was in der beständigen Fortbildung der Sprachen erscheint, das ist auch bei ihrer Entstehung aus einander geschehen, da diese ja selbst (43.) nur ein allmähliches Anderswerden seyn konnte. Ueber diese Verschiedenheit der nationellen Aneignung der Sprache liesse sich noch Vieles bemerken, wenn es nicht mein Zweck in diesem Kapitel wäre, um den Bau und das Ineinandergreifen des Ganzen zu zeigen, das Einzelne bloss andeutungsweise zu berühren.

text_version.title: Grundzüge §54 — checked German

text_version.body: This consideration becomes especially important for linguistic research as a warning against treating merely mechanical modes of explanation as sufficient and placing excessive trust in analytical procedure. Research must certainly trace the uniform course human beings take in transforming and forming language, but only with regard for the independent power capable of leaving that course or shortening it, whose mere breath gives linguistic materials an entirely different nature; one must certainly analyse and derive one thing from another, but only with the feeling that there are also true syntheses, in which idea and sound meet by a route that cannot be investigated further. Just as the stock of words and system of rules we call language are always fertilised by the living mind in thinking, speaking and recording, so investigation too must always keep both the living mind and dead language in view and follow their interaction. The individuality of nations can take such manifold paths that any attempt even to comprehend it in classes would be vain. But for the principal influences on language, only two points ever matter: whether national individuality inclines towards intellectuality at all, and from what side; and whether it inclines specifically towards intellectuality through language. For just as in daily life we encounter different degrees and kinds of need for language, feeling for language and treatment of language among individuals, so too with nations; and what manifests itself in the continual further development of languages also occurred in their emergence from one another, since this itself (43) could only have been a gradual becoming different. Much more could be observed about this diversity in the national appropriation of language, were it not my purpose in this chapter to touch on particulars only by way of indication, in order to show the structure and interlocking of the whole.

text_version.title: Grundzüge §54 — codex English, nature of language

text_version.body: This consideration becomes important for research into language pre-eminently because a warning is to be found in it against the sufficiency of merely mechanical kinds of explanation and against too great trust in analytical procedure. It must indeed trace the uniform course that man takes in altering and forming language, but only with regard to the independent power that can leave that course or shorten it, whose mere breath gives linguistic materials a wholly different nature; one must indeed analyse and derive one thing from another, but only with the feeling that there are also true syntheses, where idea and sound meet on a path that cannot be further investigated. Just as the stock of words and the system of rules that we call language are always made fruitful by the living mind in thinking, speaking and recording, so investigation too must always have the living mind and dead language at the same time before its eyes and follow their interaction. The individuality of nations can take such manifold paths that every attempt to grasp it even only in genera would be in vain. But for the principal influences upon language it always matters only to know the two points: whether it inclines at all, and from which side, to intellectuality, and whether it inclines precisely to intellectuality through language? For just as in daily life one encounters different degrees and kinds of need for language, feeling for language and treatment of language among human beings, so it is also with nations, and what appears in the constant further formation of languages also happened in their arising from one another, since this itself (43.) could only be a gradual becoming different. Much more could be remarked about this diversity of national appropriation of language if it were not my purpose in this chapter, in order to show the structure and the interlocking of the whole, merely to touch on particulars by way of indication.

text_version.title: Grundzüge §54 — revised English, nature of language

text_version.body: Da wir nunmehr die Sprache überhaupt in ihrer zwiefachen Natur betrachtet haben, als geistigen Act im Sprechen und Verstehen, und als durch diesen erzeugten, todten, zwar nie ausser dem Menschen, aber immer ausser dem Einzelnen vorhandenen Stoff (40 — 54.) , da wir ferner in ihr den Naturzusammenhang (40 — 51.) getrennt haben von der nationellen und individuellen Freiheit (52 — 54.), so gehen wir jetzt zu ihrem Verfahren im Einzelnen über. In diesem sondern sich nun zwei Dinge deutlich von einander ab, die Wörter und die Redeverbindung, als die Materie und Form der Sprache. Man muss diese Eintheilung nicht verwechseln mit der in Laute und Regeln; denn auch die Wortbildung kennt Regeln, und die Redeverbindung bedient sich bisweilen ihr eigenthümlicher Laute ; man muss vielmehr, die Rede als den Zweck der Sprache betrachtend, diese Classification dergestalt in ihrer wahren Natur fest halten, dass der eine Theil die Elemente, der andre die Verbindung der Rede behandelt. Da aber beiden der Laut gemeinsam ist, so muss die Betrachtung des Lautsystems vorausgeschickt werden.

text_version.title: Grundzüge §55 — checked German

text_version.body: Having now considered language in general in its twofold nature, as a mental act in speaking and understanding, and as dead material produced through that act, material which never exists outside human beings but always exists outside the individual (40–54); and having further distinguished within it the natural nexus (40–51) from national and individual freedom (52–54), we now turn to its procedure in detail. Here two things clearly separate from one another: words and the connection of discourse, as the matter and form of language. This division must not be confused with the division into sounds and rules, for word formation too has rules, and the connection of discourse sometimes employs sounds peculiar to it; rather, regarding discourse as the purpose of language, we must hold firmly to the true nature of this classification, so that one part treats the elements of discourse and the other their connection. Since sound is common to both, however, an examination of the sound system must precede them.

In this procedure two things now clearly separate themselves from each other, words and the combination of speech, as the matter and form of language. This division must not be confused with that into sounds and rules; for word-formation too knows rules, and the combination of speech sometimes makes use of sounds peculiar to it; rather, regarding speech as the purpose of language, one must hold fast to this classification in its true nature in such a way that the one part treats the elements of speech and the other its combination. But since sound is common to both, consideration of the system of sounds must be placed in front.
